slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Enter the US via Amazon in 2027, staged behind an ad-cost gate. Launch in stages: commit to 2027, decide 2028 on ad cost and the tariff, add retail only above 20% awareness. Approve Amazon-led entry for 2027 with a cash envelope sized to the worst-case need, not the $18M cap. Choose the US for the business it builds; keep Japan as the fallback if ad cost misses the gate.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended, staged: payback holds only while ad cost stays low. Fits the limits, but only just, and reaches $26.4M rather than $40M by 2030; pays back by 2030 only while ACoS averages below about 28.6%.

Reject: breaks all three limits, even on its own inputs. Breaks the $18M cash cap in 2029, −$20.8M in 2030; group margin 4.5% in 2027, below the 8% floor; assumes sell-through of well-known newcomers (4.5) while Onsoo's awareness band median is 2.6, below the 4.0 removal line.
Fallback: meets every limit, but a far smaller business ($7M vs $26M in 2030). Wins on cash above 25.9% ACoS; switch 2028 effort to Japan if gate 1 fails at end-2027.

alternatives_considered.option: Option A plus a national retail layer from 2029 (600 doors)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Would leave the US $11.9M short of payback in 2030 and push group margin to about 6.3% in 2029, below the 8% floor; the retail step needs its own case and a later payback date.
Not costed in the briefing pack; next step to cost it as an alternative to the 600-door national launch (Strategy, H2 2028).

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Option A payback by 2030 needs average ACoS below 28.6%; the pilot ran at 28%, the plan assumes 25%, and agency data shows a median 32% (26%–38%) at scale
If the duty rises from 15% to 25% in mid-2027, the threshold falls to about 26.9%
Volumes, fees and fixed costs are the planning team's; a weaker won would raise the threshold, a stronger one lower it
Cash turns positive only in the fourth year, so any slip pushes payback past the limit
Repeat is 29% against 31% for first-year brands and 48% in Korea; loyalty is not yet proven
The hero product's economics apply to all SKUs; no Amazon storage or return fees are given
Japan cash taken equal to its operating result (no inventory data)
The 1.3 times Amazon halo rests on a 0.71 correlation across 30 brands, which cannot show that doors drive Amazon sales
Retail sell-through of 4.5 units is optimistic unless awareness has passed 20%
Amazon-first is no guarantee: two Amazon-first peers stayed below $5M revenue
One-time US costs are expensed in the year incurred; ACoS average is weighted by sales
Synthetic benchmark data; every number from the briefing pack
